Bang & Olufsen B&O Play A1 Portable Bluetooth Speaker, Aloe, One Size This could not have been easier to set up. Well, the directions would have been easier if they separated each language instead of listing one direction in several languages in a row. Anyway, it was fully charged when I got it. I just had to turn it on, turn on the Bluetooth, then turn Bluetooth on for my Kindle fire and search for this device. I then played music from my Pandora app and my Amazon music app. I left my tablet downstairs and took the speaker upstairs and tried it in all of the rooms. The sound is great (it is a small speaker but it is very impressive). I didn't have any connection issues and the music still played even when my tablet was in sleep mode.
I am really very pleased to be able to listen to music from different services and my own music library that I keep in the Amazon cloud.

This comes with a usb cable to either charge through your laptop or a universal charger (charger not included, only the cable).
I noticed when I did charge it, it will show green when it is fully charged but then the light will go out. This confused me at first. You can't tell how much change you have left until it gets to 15 -10% left and shows red, then flashed red. You are supposed to get 24 hours of use when fully charged and that seems accurate based on what I am getting. I will play relaxation music while I sleep and I can use it two or three nights without charging unless I use it during the day.
Another feature that doesn't bother me but may be annoying to others is that there are no buttons on the speaker. It shows the small icons (power, blue tooth) and then you just press into that spot.

text_fidelity_a:
Fantom GreenDrive 500 GB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive with 2 Year Warranty GD500EU Firstly, let me say that, being a closet tech-geek. I have owned countless hard drives over the last two decades. I own stock in Seagate, so I purchased [[ASIN:B000ND75C0 Seagate FreeAgent 500 GB 3.5-Inch USB 2.0 Hard Drive ST305004FDA1E1-RK]], (only the 1TB version) from them and, to my dismay, it just stopped responding to power after a couple of months (I got it working, but it was a let-down for sure with the stock thing and all). Then, I ordered this really, really expensive, crappy paperweight here: [[ASIN:B006Y5UV4A WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black]] (same basic drive, just an earlier model no longer offered, I think), and was ready to use it for skeet practice in no time. I hated that I needed to use their software to access the data on the drive. As for the actual software, it was a total PITA. But it didn't matter because, within weeks, the damned thing crashed for good--and I wasn't even doing anything weird with it. :|

So, about three years ago, I stumbled upon the Fantom Greendrive and was, at first, kind of put-off by the apparent size (it's actually not as big as the Seagate, it turns out). I really wanted something small and portable. But, after all those issues with other drives, I really, REALLY wanted something RELIABLE. I first did some research, took a chance and ordered this drive.

DEAR GOD. IT IS MARVELOUS.

That was, as I've said, three years ago. Three years of constant use: heavy data transfer, being knocked around (even dropped on the ground a couple of times), never defragged (I got lazy cos' it's so reliable), never disk-checked, numerous power-loss and disconnection incidents....nothing can kill it! It hums along nicely no matter what you throw its way.

You don't have to ever worry about unmounting it before you turn off the power--you just unplug it and go. It's never failed me and, to be honest, that makes it better than one particular husband, in my book (the second is doing quite nicely, thank you).

The "Green" is for:

---Firstly, it doesn't take a lot of power. Nice.

---Secondly, despite being dropped a few times, it hums nicely and quietly. No loud grinding at all. I always have to check to see if it's on (which is easy because a green light shines through the grate of the front to let you know the power is on).

---Thirdly, if you have it plugged in but haven't accessed it in a while (like fifteen minutes), it will initiate a semi-hibernation, then go into a bit of a deeper hibernation after like a half hour or so (never timed it, but it's cool when it does it). So if you hear a click and a sound like the motor is clicking off, that's what you're hearing. Cooler still, the minute you click to access the drive it's ready to go--little to no wait.

It's also very fast. As drives go, mine is almost full and THREE YEARS OLD and, like I said, never defragged, yet it still runs faster for data transfer than my brand new laptop...which makes me wonder about my laptop. ;/

I actually love this drive so much, I figured with my bad luck, one day it's finally going to give up on me and quit for good. So, about a year ago I purchased the newer 2TB drive[[ASIN:B002XITVCA Micronet Technology Fantom GreenDrive 2 TB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive GD2000EUS]]for more space and extra backup. I love having the two of them because, unlike many products, Fantom keeps the peripherals consistent, so the power supplies (though upgraded to a one-piece rather than two-piece on the newer model) are interchangeable, as are the USB cables (though the 2TB, being newer, is obviously a 3.0 rather than a 2.0). Still, transferring data between the two is easy-cheesy and fast.

So, all in all, I have to tell you that, despite being an incurable tech-geek, this drive is honestly the best, most reliable, and durable piece of electronics equipment I've EVER owned.
text_fidelity_b: Fantom GreenDrive 500 GB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive with 2 Year Warranty GD500EU

text_fidelity_a:
Honeywell Home Smart Home Security Starter Kit, gray This Honeywell smart home security starter kit has a great video and is easily expandable.

When opening the box I was pleased to see that it was packaged very well. The box even has a magnetic closure. Maybe a little over the top but a nice feature to make it feel like more of a luxury product. I also have the Honeywell thermostat and that box wasn’t as nice.
Each item in the security kit was simple and clear to find since they were labeled in their own little box. There is an instruction sheet that is quite large for the info that it holds. The instructions have nice graphics and it is spaced out well so it is very easy to read. The instructions are simple for initial set up. Though I would appreciate another manual to help with the “extra” things it can do. I relied on the Honeywell videos and reviews (video and written) by other people to get it functioning with all the bells and whistles. I could see the need for a manual for those less tech savvy.

The base station could be a little smaller but it looks very nice in my kitchen and blends in very well. It’s a nice design with only one button, for the speaker. You can touch the top to check how it is working and run your finger around the top to change the volume. The camera is small and has a privacy ring that can be twisted to block the camera. It would be a nice feature if I could twist the camera from the app in case we forgot to open it when we left.
The middle mesh part is the speaker and it has a good range of volume and the sound is good.
The bottom has a light inside and it changes colors when you choose the different settings. It also lights up to help when you set up new devices.
The base has a backup battery. You will get an alert when it doesn’t have power. This has been handy when there is a storm so I know when the power goes out and when it is restored.

To start the set up I downloaded the Honeywell app. It was easy to use and is a nice looking app. The main page is very simple. When you go to the settings that’s where all the extras are.
My husband also has the app on his phone so he can use it just as I can.
Set up was very easy besides having troubles with it connecting it to my WiFi. I decided to wait till the next day and it worked after a couple tries. I don’t have a fast internet so that might be why. I haven’t had any issues with the connection since set up. Besides the WiFi wait it was about 15 minutes to set up the app and base.
The key fob was very easy to pair up and only took me a couple minutes to have it ready to use. Nice to have when a babysitter comes over.
The access sensors were very easy to install and set up. I didn’t need the extra piece. It only took me a few minutes to stick them on and pair them. I did use painters tape to attach them to my doors and frames. I am worried about the tape they have ruining my stained trim. I haven’t seen any comments about it. I also wanted to try it on other doors and windows first.
When you open a door or window in home mode it chimes and sends you an alert. When you open in away mode it will sound the alarm. I wish the door sensors were a little smaller or gray. They stand out too much on my wood trim and door. If my trim was white they wouldn’t be very noticeable.

The camera is very clear and has a wide angle so if you position it right you can see a lot. You can switch the video to full screen and the picture is still good. You are also able to zoom in on the video in the app and it has options to take a snap of the video, talk through the base or have an alarm go off. Sometimes it takes a while for the video to load or it will just turn off. I am assuming this is from my slower internet. Usually after a few tries I can get it to work. Also there is a delay in the video and the movement is jumpy, this could be due to the slower internet also. You still get a good picture of who is there. I was impressed with the night vision.

The motion detection is a nice feature when you are away. I have been trying to figure out the best setting while we are at home. It will send me alerts all the time when we are home. Most of the alerts are during the people detection time. Maybe because our camera covers so much of our main area. I do like that how the people detection can let me know who is in the house and I don’t have to look at the video. When it detects motion it will take a short video clip and save them below the live video. You can scroll down to look at the older ones. It looks like the clips are saved for a day. The people detection is limited to 2 hours. But I did notice that you could set it for the morning then when that time was over you could change it for later in the day. You would have to remember to change it but good to know if you wanted it on for longer or multiple times in the day. Not sure why they don’t have an option for more time.

The geofencing didn’t work well for me. It would switch to away mode even when the phone was close to it. We’ve decided to turn that feature off. It’s easy enough to turn it to away with the app, key fob, or talk to it. We are at home a lot so it makes more sense to do it manually. But I could see it being a great feature for people gone more during the day.

The kids like the Alexa feature that it comes with. They can ask the weather, time, kids jokes. I use it for the timer and to ask it questions. We had problems with playing songs. It wanted us to subscribe to amazon music. We have found other ways of playing music but it’s not very easy. Alexa seems limited but still useful. This is my first Alexa enable device so hard to compare.

I like that the security base links to my Honeywell thermostat (it was very easy to pair it) and I can tell Alexa to turn it off or change the temperature or use the same app. I would like to get other devices that link to it. This is a great starter kit and I like that it is expandable for your needs.

You are able to do two way taking with the app. It’s not always easy to understand and you have to talk slower.

The box says you get free 24-hour cloud storage. I’m not sure if that’s for the video clips or what you are actually storing. I haven’t found where the cloud is accessed.

Overall it is easy to use and looks nice. It’s nice that you can have a security system that is easy to use and it doesn’t have a monthly fee. I don’t usually need all the security features that this security system offers but it’s nice to have it set up and ready for when I do.
text_fidelity_b: Honeywell Home Smart Home Security Starter Kit, gray

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link USB WiFi Adapter for PC(TL-WN725N), N150 Wireless Network Adapter for Desktop - Nano Size WiFi Dongle for Windows 11/10/7/8/8.1/XP/ Mac OS 10.9-10.15 Linux Kernel 2.6.18-4.4.3, 2.4GHz Only At first I struggled to get this adapter to work with Linux. I plugged it into the computer --- nothing. Then I went to the website and found the driver package, which had to be downloaded, then followed the instructions to install it from the command line (along with some other items had to be installed as well). I tried installing the beta and stable driver packages, and the installation failed both times.

I had about given up. Even though I bought the adapter on sale, I considered returning it. I did another search for TP-Link drivers for Linux, and found a suggestion in the replies to an article on installing WiFi drivers:

Turn off the computer, plug in the dongle, then reboot the computer.

. . .

That did it. The system loaded drivers and the adapter worked fine, and worked much better than the old adapter I was replacing. I did have to type in the password to reconnect to the WiFi network, but that was it. Works great now.

That worked with an Ubuntu-based version of Linux. Getting it to work with Debian Linux was a little different. I did a search for "wifi" in Synaptic package manager, and found and installed a package called "firmware-realtek." (You may have to add or check "non-free" repositories for it to show up.) I rebooted and now it works great with Debian Linux.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link USB WiFi Adapter for PC(TL-WN725N), N150 Wireless Network Adapter for Desktop - Nano Size WiFi Dongle for Windows 11/10/7/8/8.1/XP/ Mac OS 10.9-10.15 Linux Kernel 2.6.18-4.4.3, 2.4GHz Only

text_fidelity_a:
Razer Kraken BT Kitty Edition: Bluetooth 5.0-40ms Low Latency Connection - Custom-Tuned 40mm Drivers - Beamforming Microphone - Powered Chroma - Quartz Pink The Razer Kraken BT Kitty headset is not a serious gaming headset. The lighting effects and cat ears look cool, and it’s Bluetooth so no wires like the original Kraken Kitty -- those are the big pros.

Razer Synapse does not recognize the headset, so if you want to customize it, two different phone apps are needed.

The Razer Chroma RGB app handles lighting options. The Razer Audio app handles sound settings, firmware updates, and changing the auto shutoff timer.

Do I really want to use my phone to manage my gaming headset? No. I consider having to use my phone while I’m playing a game on my computer to be a hassle!

I did find that I could customize the lighting effects with my phone, unpair the headphones from my phone and then pair them with my computer to keep the lighting effects while using with my computer. But that is also a hassle, considering Razer has a program meant to handle this!

Sound quality is just okay -- it’s not great. I’m not an audiophile so it works for me, but I have less expensive headphones that have better playback, even to my inexperienced ears. The headphones do not have ANC and I miss that a lot.

The controls are basic, a volume wheel and a power button. The power button can be used to pause and play, just hold it in for two seconds and let go, and the music will pause. Hold in for two seconds and let go to resume.

The headphones don’t have a 3.5mm audio jack, they are only Bluetooth. The charging cable is micro USB.

I have the Kraken Kitty wired headset, and I wanted a wireless version because once I started using Bluetooth headphones, I couldn’t stand being chained at my desk by a wire. But I feel like Razer wanted to appeal to women gamers -- make it pink, slap on kitty ears -- and didn’t focus as much on quality or function.
text_fidelity_b: Razer Kraken BT Kitty Edition: Bluetooth 5.0-40ms Low Latency Connection - Custom-Tuned 40mm Drivers - Beamforming Microphone - Powered Chroma - Quartz Pink

text_fidelity_a:
FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium) I love my FiiO X5 2nd gen player! I love that it has two micro SD card slots (which I use both for a total of 192GB of storage space, with one 64GB card and one 128GB card), because I can put two separate sets of music in there and go back and forth between the cards depending on my musical needs (for example, on the 64GB card, I put recently purchased tracks, and for the entirety of my rest of my library, I put those tracks on the 128GB card). It allows me faster access to my newer stuff, which I want to listen to now, vs. randomizing the rest of my music from the other card.

The sound is unheard of (ha ha, sorry for the pun). Nothing compares to the quality of sound that comes out of this little machine, for its size and price. Pair it with a set of high quality hi-fi headphones and some FLAC music files, and you've got yourself an insane little music machine. You'll never go back to Apple or another brand of music player. You'll find yourself hooking it up to your home sound system and playing all of your music through it. I can't say enough for the sound quality. You WILL notice a difference between crummy .mp3 files and other low-quality sound files. You WILL find yourself craving FLAC files, and you will go wherever you can to find them. You might even start converting your entire CD music collection into FLAC, even though you'd already converted them all to .mp3. You WILL find yourself hoping that someday soon, Amazon will start offering FLAC files instead of .mp3s! (HINT HINT NUDGE NUDGE!) ;) Seriously, though, you probably haven't realized how GOOD your music will sound until you listen to it on this FiiO X5 2nd gen. Even the .mp3s sound better. Especially if you use noise cancelling headphones.

I like that you can adjust the configuration and tell it which buttons to remain active when the screen is off, depending on your preferences. I also like that there are several preset themes to choose from. The screen is easy to read and nicely displays album art.

The unit itself has a wonderful weight to it given the aluminum shell. The volume wheel moves easily and there is a slight tactile feedback click. That wheel controls both the song volume and song selection, depending on which screen you're on when you use it. The power on button has a tiny LED light that's blue when it's running and red when it's charging. There are volume up/down buttons beneath the power button and those buttons are some of the buttons that you can choose whether or not to have active while the screen is off.

I'm not sure if I there's a firmware update that needs to be done that could change this, but there are a couple of things that are pretty bothersome in general about this unit:

1) There is no way to search for a song. If, like me, you have more than 5,000 songs, it's impossible to sit and scroll through each album/folder to find a specific song. I suppose if you're some kind of major organization guru (which I thought I was, but apparently not at this), it would be possible to arrange your music folders into genres or some other category to make it easier to get to the exact music you need to play, but if you've moved over from iTunes like I have, you're probably real spoiled with the ability to view songs either by artist, album, song name, etc., as well as the ability to do a search. Here, you're pretty much on your own, depending on how you've got your music library set up. Having purchased most of my music here on Amazon, it's all arranged by artist name in individual folders. I have several hundred folders set up like this, and scrolling through everything with that scroll wheel can take a very, very long time to find the one thing you're looking for.

2) The unit can be quite SLOW to respond to your clicks. It is not touch-screen, and when you click on a button to change tracks forward/backward or to change from looking at what's playing into another option, such as a list of the songs on the album, it can be quite sluggish. Again, if you're used to using an iPod, you'll be frustrated with the lack of responsiveness of this unit. Again, I keep hoping a firmware update will come out that addresses this.

3) Whenever you add music to your micro SD card(s) [NOTE: There is NO onboard storage, it's purely on whatever card(s) you insert into it] you have to completely update your whole media library. This can take a long time depending on how much music you have, so keep this in mind and don't expect to add music and listen to it immediately. In other words, plan ahead for this :)

4) It's not as user friendly as the typical Apple products you may be used to. You'll get used to it, but don't expect the polished feel because of issues like #1 and #2, above.

5) Playlists are not straightforward. Yes, you can be playing a song and add it to a playlist that resides on one of your SD cards. However, importing playlists can be tricky and you may find yourself looking to the internet to help convert your existing playlists from your prior player. Expect to spend some time on this unless you're totally okay with starting over from scratch (I wasn't okay with this). Also, any playlists that you save to your SD card that you've hand-converted do not show up as a playlist on the FiiO. Instead, you have to navigate to the file on your player as if you were looking for a song, and play it as if you were playing a song. Only playlists you've created on the machine show up in the Playlist section, not playlists you've brought in from elsewhere. There is no 'import' feature or anything fancy like that, so you're pretty much on your own unless you add a song one at a time to Playlist 1, Playlist 2, etc. (I do not yet see a way to rename these as there is no keyboard function on this machine, so you're stuck with those names).

I think with time, the FiiO's software will catch up closer to what you're seeing from the high-visibility media consumer based music players, but right now with this X5 you should be more concerned with how WONDERFUL your music sounds vs the issues associated with the frumpy software that comes with it.
text_fidelity_b: FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium)

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 is STM Lens, Lens Only I really bought a Canon DSLR (vs Nikon, or any of the mirrorless Cameras) for this lens. I needed a low distortion very wide lens for real estate videos and I also needed image stabilization and quiet focusing. I don't think there is any other lens from any manufacturer that satisfies all of those things except this one. (Sigma has the 10-20mm but no stabilization, lower optical quality, and more money! Tamaron - 10-24 - same story. And so on ).
GOOD: Excellent optical quality for the price. This lens is noticeably sharper and has less distortion at 10mm than my kit lens 18-135mm has at 18mm. Stabilization works very well. Focusing is very fast and silent. I don't hear it even with the built in mic when shooting video (on a Canon 70D). Extremely lightweight and fairly compact.

BAD: Maximum Aperture. This is NOT a fast lens. F/4.5 maximum is not that great and you lose it pretty quickly as you zoom in since the max aperture ranges from 4.5 - 5.6. You need to have some decent light to shoot with this lens. But given the lack of competition in super wide stabilized silent EF-S lenses (or any Canon mount lens) and the price of anything vaguely similar, I think it's a reasonable compromise.

Note: At this price, you can't really call it a knock, but it'd be nice if it came with the lens hood. You can get a clone lens hood for $10 or so.

ALSO: Canon has now updated their EOS Utility software for this lens.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 is STM Lens, Lens Only

SAMSUNG 49-Inch CHG90 144Hz Curved Gaming Monitor (LC49HG90DMNXZA) – Super Ultrawide Screen QLED Computer Monitor, 3840 x 1080p Resolution, 1ms Response, FreeSync 2 with HDR,Black Wow this thing is wide. Works great. I recommend reading the instructions before you unpack anything. It can sound like an obvious or easy thing, but I felt like I had to unpack this in the driveway because I wasn't sure I was going to have room inside to deal with it all. It's closer to a couch than a monitor in this respect.

This is about twice the size of any monitor I'd ever unpacked, and the curve presents an interesting challenge. They don't want you to just lay it face down on the floor to deal with assembly, because the arch puts too much stress on the center. The packing materials are designed for this. You can leave it in the foam packing when you remove the box, and it'll hold it steady while you get everything put together and plugged in.

Most of the assembly is for the mount on the back. It's like putting together a Portal gun or something. From the back, it really looks like it was designed by Aperture Science. The main support attachment from monitor to mounting hardware is excellent. Easy to attach, but strongly supportive. After adding some rings and back plates, it's almost ready. There are channels in the stand for cables if you pay attention to the fine print in the instructions before you get too far along (oops).

The most questionable part to me is a plate that goes all across the lower back and covers up the ports. I'm thinking of it as optional. It makes things look nice if you spend a lot of time looking at the wrong side of your monitor, and also never mess with your cords or ports. It's also kind of huge, like the rest of the monitor, so if you aren't using it it presents something of a dilemma whether to keep it around or not.

The swivel mount on the back is really smooth and makes it easy to orient it with a light touch, and it stays put. This is elegant engineering. Getting just the right balance and tension.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 49-Inch CHG90 144Hz Curved Gaming Monitor (LC49HG90DMNXZA) – Super Ultrawide Screen QLED Computer Monitor, 3840 x 1080p Resolution, 1ms Response, FreeSync 2 with HDR,Black

text_fidelity_a:
Joby Gorillamobile Ori for iPad (GM12-01AM) Multipositional Protective Lightweight Aluminum Case Silver UPDATE: This also works very well with an HP Touchpad. It's slighly smaller than the ipad so the fit is not as tight, but still quite stable. If you position the Touchpad correctly the on/off button works fine, and the volume button sort of works (can lower the volume easily but raising it requires a bit more effort).

Original review:
This is probably the most useful accessory I've every used for the iPad. Truly amazing in how it can be folded and unfolded to provide ease of use regardless of how you're using the iPad.

All the options make for a bit of a learning curve, however. I tried to follow the diagrams in the user's guide, but didn't really "get" how to use this until I watched the manufacturer's video. Highly recommend that as a guide to how to get the most out of this stand.

I'm especially pleased with being able to use it as a stand for viewing a movie (the position they call "Popcorn and a Movie" in the manual). Excellent when more than one person want to view the screen.

I can't comment with any degree of certainty as to it's longevity since I've only been using it for a few days, but it seems very sturdy. I'll update the review should that assumption prove faulty.

My big question is whether it will fit the iPad 2. Clearly it will cause problems with the cameras, but it is such a tight fit with the iPad 1 (which is a good thing in a case for security) that I'm hopeful that it will work with the iPad 2 with (perhaps) a bit of padding to make up for the thinner profile. I'll update with my experiences with the iPad 2 later this month once I have one in hand.

But regardless of fitting other models, this is an outstanding accessory for the iPad 1. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Joby Gorillamobile Ori for iPad (GM12-01AM) Multipositional Protective Lightweight Aluminum Case Silver

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS C100PA-DB02 10.1-inch Touch Chromebook Flip (1.8GHz, 4GB Memory, 16GB eMMC, Google OS), All Metal Body When my dog chewed up the cord to my 2012 Samsung Chromebook, instead of getting a new cord, I decided maybe it was time to get a new Chromebook. After reading all the "top five" reviews I could find, I decided to get this ASUS Chromebook Flip because of the excellent build quality compared to the others and the features. My partner has a Windows-based ASUS tablet this same size that he has really loved, so I knew the ASUS brand would be dependable. However, I didn't realize that this one would be the same size as his, but had I been thinking clearly I would have realized I would not be happy with the smaller keyboard size.

When the Flip came, I was definitely impressed with its build. Everything the reviewers said was true. I was thinking about sending it back, but then DP mentioned that he wished he had an ASUS like the Flip that could run Linux; apparently, he's going to sell his other ASUS because he's quitting Windows and the other ASUS machine has something proprietary about it that prevents him from being able to install Linux on it. Other than that, he loves it. He said he didn't want a Chromebook. But I searched and discovered that Linux CAN be put on the Flip and told him so, so he happily took it. I don't think he realized, either, how great a Chromebook is when you're cloud-centric like I am, and like he's increasingly becoming, so he casually mentioned to me last night that he might not even put Linux on it. There's no reason why he couldn't boot Linux from a flash drive, I don't think, if he wants to leave the Chrome as the main system OS.

I have tried the different options that come with them to get a better fit and stay in my ear tighter to no avail.

For outdoor activity, I cannot wear these. They fall out of my ear and I lose them. However, indoors I love the Alexa integration. If they could make them in a way they stay in my ear, they would be perfect. Last night, one fell out and went into the garbage disposer. Luckily, it was not on and water wasn't running or it would have been gone.

As they work loose quickly, sound quality and volume diminishes. They do have good bass response when tightly fitted in your ear. If I am sitting still listening to music or an audio book, they work great. As I start to move around, they loosen up and sound poor and are at risk of falling out.

Overall, I do have a use for them. I love the ability to use Alexa. I wish they could do Alexa independent of a mobile device via wi-fi, which they cannot. I love the ability to recharge them from the case when traveling. The case is hard shell and very protective of the earbuds. The case is probably the best part of the product.

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Electronics UN55MU6300 55-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2017 Model) I use this as a computer monitor for my photo workstation. I use it to preview images in a catalog. At the distance used there is light fall off in the corners, so if you have the funds a curved monitor might work better for the same purpose. For my needs it is not perfect but good enough for a professional adobe display. According to my calibrator this does Adobe 87%. The IPS display it replaced was slightly higher % wise but had an annoying red color cast that I could not calibrate out.

Out of the box I got 4:2:0, I needed to get an NVIDIA 10 series card to do full 4:4:4. This did nothing for color space but did remove annoying purple "frigging" around text. You NEED a card that can do HDMI 1.4 out in order to use this as a computer monitor at 4K. In which case a NVIDIA 10 Series or AMD equivalent.

As a TV it is perfect. The low end reach of the speakers was surprising, I was going to get pc speakers but the one built in are good enough. The included apps work fine.

My only issue is the standby nag screen. If you have the TV on and turn the computer off, the TV might go in to "No signal" screen which does not seem to go away. I had the input set to PC, it should know to turn itself off. You need the remote to change the sound and turn the monitor on and off.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Electronics UN55MU6300 55-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2017 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
MOTOROLA XOOM Android Tablet (10.1-Inch, 32GB, Wi-Fi) I used to think tablet computers were just for dorks like that guy on Modern Family and for people that want everyone to see how hip and up-to-date they are. But after nabbing a pile of these for the one team of surveyors at work, I'm pleasantly surprised to see how many real business applications these can tackle.

I won't go into too much detail - there are legions of people contributing to forums and reviews on such matters. What I do hate, however - and this is why it gets only four stars - is that the SD card is still not write-enabled. My buddy working for Google swears he has a software-enabled version that does, but the public does not. Yet, at least. So what's the hold up?, 'cause that is a serious deal-breaker.

On the other hand, Apple's version doesn't even have an SD card slot. Heck, it has nothing that isn't proprietary. iPad was never on the table for me, and probably never will be. Why anyone would go that direction when open source is available cheaper is beyond me. Anyway, to each his own.

My only other issue is that it kept resetting itself on me during casual browsing, driving me nuts, even after a factory reset with no futher modifications. After installing a new browser, I no longer have that problem, thank God.

VIZIO Sound Bar for TV, 28” 2.1 Surround Sound System for TV with Wireless Subwoofer and Bluetooth, Channel Home Theater Sound Bar – Remote SB2821-D6 The first delivery had subwoofer that was dead on arrival. No power.

They sent a replacement. It works great. Music streaming from my phone or computer by bluetooth sounds great. Better than my Bose.

If you want instruction on how to operate this thing properly look at the copied review below. This was helpful.

One other or two were somewhat helpful.

The instructions they put in the package gets the thing on but doesn't tell you how to operate it.

FYI:

"Please handle this unit with care when taking it out of the box. The sub-woofer in particular, which has the speaker cone located on the bottom of the sub-woofer. If you grab it from the bottom, you could damage it very easily. When set up properly, I found this Sound Bar to have very good sound. However it did take me awhile to reach this state. Because like most men, I know everything, I skipped through the instructions, plugged in the sound bar and was extremely disappointed in the quality of the sound. Here are a few tips to make things easier. If you're doing a horizontal installation in front of the TV at ear level, the sound button the the bar should be located on top, and the small lights that show volume level, etc., should be located on the left when facing your TV. That way the speakers are facing you. Also, I had a difficult time finding the audio settings on my TV to turn off the internal speakers and use the external speakers. Naturally I thought, heck just turn down the volume on the TV speakers to zero and it should be the same thing. Wrong !! You have to find and turn on the external speakers, and turn off the internal speakers for this sound bar to work properly. The sound bar does come with a remote, which is an absolute necessity no matter which sound bar you order. Read the instruction manual carefully, as you have to use the 'previous" and "next" buttons to adjust the Sub-woofer, Bass and Treble settings. Since I know everything, I naturally assumed the volume up and down buttons would adjust these settings. Wrong !! Also, there are buttons to enable TruVolume, and TruSurround HD, but the manual doesn't clarify exactly when to use these settings or what they actually do. I suggest trying both settings and see if you notice any difference in sound quality. I've read a few complaints about the bass not being that strong, but I found it to be excellent. I wonder if these users had the sub-woofer in the correct location, and if they figured out how to raise the sub-woofer level using the remote, and if the sub-woofer stopped working and needed to be "re-linked". I had to re-link mine, and although the instructions could be better, got the sub-woofer working properly in a few minutes. With the sub-woofer is turned on, located in the right area, and adjusted with the remote, you should be very happy with the results. Why only 4 stars for this product? First, the instruction manual could have been more informative about the settings on the remote, and second the ergonomics of the remote are in my opinion very bad. The volume adjustment in particular is usually an up and down toggle on every remote I ever used, but not on this one. The technical designer genius of this remote decided to put a big square "enter/play/pause button between the up and down volume adjustment buttons. Hence adjusting the volume by feel is the worst of any remote I've ever had. That being said, once set up properly, you should be extremely happy with the sound quality of this sound bar."
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO Sound Bar for TV, 28” 2.1 Surround Sound System for TV with Wireless Subwoofer and Bluetooth, Channel Home Theater Sound Bar – Remote SB2821-D6

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th) I've been an avid fan of ebooks since the long gone days of the Rocket and the eBookman, and a fan of the Kindle since the very beginning. This is miles and away the best there has ever been. It is a luxury model, no doubt, but oh is it luxurious.

I like:
The weight. Even in the case it's very light, though if it gets much lighter I'll worry about it blowing away in a strong wind.
The size. It's not going to get much smaller without shrinking the screen.
The interface. I'm sorry, I like buttons. Call me old. I never bent back the spine of a book (horrors) so I can't compare the feel of this to that, but I can say it's nice for a long reading session. The touch screen takes a bit of getting used to, but the tutorial will guide a new user. The tutorial is intrusive at first, but provides useful information and goes away quickly. I will suggest customizing the screen. I hated the default, but you get a lot of options to make it just the way you want.
The lighting is now all but invisible. I was unhappy that you can't completely turn it off as you could with the Nook Glowlight, and turning it down casts an odd yellow light over the page, but it's so even now as to be so unintrusive I barely notice going from sunlight to tunnel on the bus home. With the Nook I'd be thrown out of the book to go turn on the light. With the Kindle, I can keep reading without a pause. It does not have adaptive lighting, but I'm not sure it needs it.
The download speed. I don't know if it's supposed to be faster than the Kindle Keyboard (the last one I had with 3G) but it certainly seems that way.
The battery life. Maybe with this thing going for months we'll finally hear an end to the "but my dead tree doesn't run out of power" nonsense.
Next in series. When you're almost done with a book, it tells you where the story continues. Now the next feature I want, and if it does this I haven't seen it yet, is an alert when the next book in a series I'm following is published. Yes, FictFact is great, but I'm greedy and want it right on the device.

I don't like:
It's not waterproof. There was a lot of hope it would be after the Nook went that route.
It's not solar, yet, but there are rumors of a solar cover coming soon.
It doesn't support Audible and the excellent immersive reading between ebook and audiobook. I have a weird love of that feature, seeing what changed print to audio.
Recommended Content and Reading Lists. I shut this feature off. The information seems scattered at best and gave me no useful information, especially considering how precious screen real estate is.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th)

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlaySport (Zx3) HD Waterproof Pocket Video Camera (Purple) There's a lot to like about the Playsport. For one, it's very easy to use as a point and shoot should be. The picture quality is certainly fine for just about anybody's use, save for those who really like blowing their pictures up large. It's very fast to move between photos and movie--a few thumb moves is all it takes. The same for toggling between the movie quality. Which means if you suddenly want to grab a still photo while videoing or are worried about recording room and want to drop down a notch or two in quality, you can do so without missing a lot of action. The zoom is a 3X, which is serviceable. I'd prefer longer and I'm sure the next version will offer a longer zoom, but as I use this for quick shots of the family and not for event shooting, the 3X is rarely an issue in terms of not being adequate.

Transfer of files is easy and fast (I use a Mac) and all the cables come bundled with it. Yes, you read that right--it ships with all the needed cables.

Because it is so small and slim, and held in that vertical position, it can get a bit shaky and you'll need to pay attention to keeping it steady, more so than larger cameras or ones you hold with two hands horizontally. The sound pickup is fine save that wind noise can be a problem on windy days--it'll wash out a good deal of the speaking sound.

It feels rugged out of the box and the number of times I've dropped it, including just recently while chasing my boy and his friend around the corner of the house and getting my foot caught in the extension cord of the Halloween decorations. I watched the camera skid across several feet of concrete sidewalk but it was none the worse for wear.

It's slimness makes it a great pocket camera--one of those where it's defined as such not because you can cram it into your pocket and walk around like you have a grapefruit in there but where it slips right in and you barely notice it. That's one of the reasons it's become the camera I take most often when I know I won't need a larger zoom or a flash.

I haven't tried the underwater aspect in actual underwater conditions (snorkeling, say), but a few practice photos in the pool shows it takes pretty sharp photos in that environment. But I'll leave the gauging of that aspect to those more well-versed in such a need.

In the end, it's a great little camera and as mentioned, it's quickly become the one I carry along most often when we're just heading out for some family fun. For post-dusk indoor, I take a Canon elph and for events or hiking a Canon IS with a 12x zoom and a tele-converter. But for playing games in the yard, birthday parties, classroom events, etc.--the Kodak has become the go-to camera.

highly recommended
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlaySport (Zx3) HD Waterproof Pocket Video Camera (Purple)

text_fidelity_a: Kindle E-reader, 6" Glare-Free Touchscreen Display, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation – 7th) I was really looking forward to the touch screen, but it's ended up being really annoying. I like to read holding the Kindle one handed, but even holding it with both hands, or even holding it in one hand and using the index finger of the other hand (the most careful way to tap the touch screen) when I tap the right side to advance a page, it often jumps forward several pages. And it is incredibly annoying to have to page back to the page I was trying to get to in the first place. Jerks me right out of the book. It's annoying enough that I wish I'd kept my old, non touch screen Kindle. It seems to be confined to page turning, so when I need to use the on screen keyboard it works great. And that's the reason I upgraded. Still, having a hard to use keyboard is *much* preferable to this "jump ahead several pages" thing. Oh well, live and learn.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle E-reader, 6" Glare-Free Touchscreen Display, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation – 7th)

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa "Set up in minutes"?? Not really. There are no actual detailed instructions included. I tried scanning the QR code that was provided in the little pamphlet, and that was not helpful. This ended up being extremely frustrating to set up. I could take a wild guess that I was supposed put the lithium batteries in the back of the camera. I would not have known that the little QR code inside the camera where the batteries go was something that I had to scan to set up the camera. Anyway, without going into detail, if Amazon provided some simple, basic instructions with photos that show step by step, it would save the customer a ton of fumbling around. Then it might have been an easy set up. I had to call for support, and by the time I got a support person on the phone I was pretty irritated. The reason I decided to buy this camera is the "two-year battery life." Note: these are not rechargeable batteries. We'll see how long the batteries last. Prior to this, I got a Eufy Solocam, also wireless (and much, much easier to set up), and it had rechargeable batteries advertised to last 4 months, but they lasted 4 weeks. A feature that is missing with the Blink camera, that I liked on the Eufy camera, is the AI feature to recognize humans. Without the AI feature, the Blink is recording non-human motion, such as animals and vehicles.

Update: The description advertises customized zones for motion detection. The camera takes a photo what it sees, and in motion settings, you gray out areas that you do not want the camera to detect motion. It does NOT work. I tried resetting it several times, and the camera recorded and sent me an alert of motion detected that was squarely in the grayed out area. Without this feature actually working, and without the AI feature to detect humans, the camera is recording every motion in the entire viewable area, ignoring the areas that I grayed out. I am returning this camera.
text_fidelity_b: Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
Senso Bluetooth Headphones, Best Wireless Sports Earphones w/Mic IPX7 Waterproof HD Stereo Sweatproof Earbuds for Gym Running Workout 8 Hour Battery Noise Cancelling Headsets (Black Red) I have had way too many sets of headphones. Mostly because my dog eats them if they are within reach. While I still have not found the perfect headset with these, they come pretty close.

Durability and battery Life - Way too early to tell. I'll update this after a few months.

Noise Canceling- Let’s get something straight - if you put your fingers in your ears, they will cancel noise. That's called passive noise canceling, or simply, blocking outside noise. True active noise canceling head phones are over the ear, and usually very expensive. These head phones do a pretty good job passively blocking outside noise by fitting very well to the ear and being angled correctly.

Sound - Everyone has different tastes when it comes to what they like to hear. Some headphones have good or bad ranges from high to low. But it is the quality of the range that matters. For instance, I like to hear bass, and to me there is nothing worse than a tinny am radio sound. These definitely have bass, but it's a bit muddy. The good news is I was able to adjust the equalizer on my phone to clean it up, mostly. Overall all though, for the price, the sound quality is pretty darn good.

Fit & Hold - They Fit and stay put! The best part of these headphones is they fit my ears perfectly. The part that goes around the ear has a wire going through it, unlike so many others. This allows you to mold the over ear wires exactly to you ear and they do not fall out. None of the last several sets I had do this, and it is an enormous benefit.

Controls - The are typical up and down volume and a center button that is used for on, off, hold, answer, etc. I wish the volume buttons were reversed, but that's just being picky. They announce power on, power off and connected. Sadly, they do not announce battery life.

Appearance – Meh. They are a bit big and boxy, but I don’t know how that‘s different from having white things hanging out of your ears for $200.00

Overall - I am giving this 5 starts not because they are the best headphones. I am giving them 5 starts because they check off almost all of my boxes and the price it great. So, 5 stars for overall function and price.

Note: I paid full price for these and I was not asked to review them. Also, if you like this review, please indicate so below. Thanks.
text_fidelity_b: Senso Bluetooth Headphones, Best Wireless Sports Earphones w/Mic IPX7 Waterproof HD Stereo Sweatproof Earbuds for Gym Running Workout 8 Hour Battery Noise Cancelling Headsets (Black Red)

text_fidelity_a:
Motorola T200TP Talkabout Radio, 3 Pack This is a nice little set of radios, improved from my last three-pack of similarly priced Motorolas, but has some room for improvement.

Goods:

+ Good size - small enough, but big enough to fit in your hand comfortably like a radio should. Yes, it could be smaller, but at some point you don't really want smaller.

+ Some basic options to customize, mostly the noises the radios make. LCD screen shows you what you need to know.

+ Batteries can be charged while in the radios via standard Micro USB adapters - two are included. One charges one radio while the other charges two simultaneously.

+ Belt clip included. Head sets can be added.

Bad:

- While it's great that the battery packs can be charged via USB and the chargers are accepted worldwide (whereas my previous set for work had barrel connections to the charger and I burnt one out the first night I tried to charge due to being in Europe, the battery/charger setup is still imperfect for two reasons:

1) Battery packs are not three separate batteries that could be charged with other chargers and switched with other batteries (think Eneloop). My Garmin topo GPS came with actual rechargeable batteries that could be used elsewhere. This makes sense when you want to be able to carry standard alkaline batteries for emergencies/backup. These battery packs are great that they can be replaced with AA when necessary, but not as good as standard, replaceable rechargeable batteries (but you can use rechargeable batteries as your backup batteries).

2) N-MH doesn't make sense for this application because these are the type of batteries that develop a "memory". If you use these every day for work, then you want to recharge them every night. Actually, you would be inclined to recharge every time you want to use them, period, to be sure you get the most from the batteries. But because of the memory, you really want to discharge them fully. The appropriate type of battery would be Li-ion, because they would be chargeable every night AND would last longer. This is the biggest negative to this rig. If the battery packs were Li-ion, I would not care that they are packs versus separate batteries.

- Belt clip should be taken off to remove battery cover without beating the two up. This is apparently an obvious issue to the manufacturer because they have a protective piece of plastic between the two for shipment.

Neutral (strange):

Two standard USB chargers included, at 500mA output each (1A would be minimum standard and expected these days, but whatever; they may have done this to avoid overcharging overnight). Both have the same rated input, but the output is the same (samex2 on the 2 output charger). That actually doesn't make sense, unless the single charger is half as efficient (or they are just too lazy to change the nameplate). Not really sure what's up with that, but I sort of like the 2-output charger. I expect most people have so many USB chargers laying around that they'll use whatever is at hand anyway vice these.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola T200TP Talkabout Radio, 3 Pack

text_fidelity_a:
iPad Pro 10.5 Case with Wireless Keyboard, Janvvoo Ultra-Thin Lightweight Bluetooth Keyboard with Magnetically Intelligent Switch and Multi-Angle Stand for Apple iPad Pro 10.5 inch Tablet I have owned this shredder for over six years, and it has endured some heavy use. It is the second home-shredder I've owned, and it is much the better of the two. It is heavy enough that it doesn't tip over, but not so heavy it can't be hauled from room to room by someone moderately strong. The front compartment holding the shredded paper is easily removed--in an identical fashion to our dehumidifier's bucket. You pull on it and the bucket comes out with a forward motion. The sound the shredder makes when in action is loud, as one would expect, but not so loud that you need protective ear plugs, such as for when you are near a kitchen blender, blow dryer, leaf blower or lawn mower.

The main thing to be careful about is to not get impatient and overload the shredder blades. Yes, you can use the backup function to try and back out paper you have overloaded it with, but it is a pain. Secondly, be sure and feed paper in straight. If you feed it in crooked, that, too, is a prescription for a jam.

When I am shredding, I lay down either a bed sheet or a tarp and set the shredder in the middle of it. This helps me corral the scraps of shredded paper flying around when I empty the bucket into a trash bag. Another option is to shred in your garage or basement, if you have such spaces, and use a [[ASIN:B00005AXI1 Shop-Vac]] to clean up afterwards. If you do it inside your house, plan on having to use a regular vacuum to clean up after each use, because a mess is almost unavoidable no matter how careful you are since this shredder is turning private papers into confetti. That's great for the shredder's intended purpose, but it does have a tendency to give whatever room you are using a strong resemblance to Times Square on New Year's Eve.
text_fidelity_b: iPad Pro 10.5 Case with Wireless Keyboard, Janvvoo Ultra-Thin Lightweight Bluetooth Keyboard with Magnetically Intelligent Switch and Multi-Angle Stand for Apple iPad Pro 10.5 inch Tablet

text_fidelity_a:
Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender The tech geek in our household kept telling me there was nothing we could do to improve on the truly horrendous wireless internet service we have. He said we were stuck with the ISP we have and with their router (which he has in the far back bedroom, on the other side of our apartment from the pricey smart TV I haven't been able to use for anything but watching cable news). I haven't been able to stream anything from Amazon Prime, nor can I access the internet at all through the TV. So in complete frustration, without telling him, I ordered the Securifi Almond. Price was one factor in my decision, but I knew I wasn't going to be able to depend on him to help me set anything up and I'm not all that tech savvy.

One of the attractive selling points of this router is that it can be used either as a router or as a range extender. I planned to set it up as a range extender to see if I could get a better signal near my TV, but also had in mind that I might be able to persuade a certain somebody to try it as our router in place of the one that I feel like is defective (or just crummy) from our ISP.

I set it up myself. I just followed the installation on screen, and it was a snap. Fortunately, I knew what our log-in info was for our network so I didn't have to ask for help. I wasn't sure how it was supposed to work with the ethernet cable, so I plugged the Almond into the LAN port of of my TV and into one of the ports with a TV icon on the router. Then I tested it. Wow. The streaming is so much better than it was that I signed up for Netflix and started binging on "House of Cards." I still have the rotating download timer come up once or twice during an episode, but it gets done pretty quickly and the episode finishes playing. Before, I couldn't even load an episode or, worse, it would play a minute then completely drop the connection to the internet.

So I'm quite happy. This is a sleek little baby that works. I can see at a glance that I'm connected, which is reassuring. I haven't yet tried it in its router mode, but as a range extender it works great. You need to use the little stowaway stylus that comes with it when you're selecting onscreen functions, but as long as you remember to re-stow it, you've always got it handy if you need it.
text_fidelity_b: Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation Another reviewer mentioned these issues, but I was impulsive and bought it anyways. They are all true.
- I spend a good deal of time adjusting the sensibility settings and using the brackets (both V and H) to reduce false positives, but they are still too many. My door is about 25-30' from the road and if a truck passes, even small cars, "motion detected". You stop giving importance for the sensor.
- I try to answer motion but it takes so long to load (I have an S8, with good wifi) and I got a connection problem way too often. If wasn't another false positive (as usually is), I would have missed the person lurking.
- The recording starts too late. when you go see the recorded video (because you were not able to answer the false positive motion), the video starts way too long after the movement started.
- regarding payments: I have a Piper camera that records up to 1,000 24s videos for free, overwriting after that. It works great. It always worked. Why Ring enforce additional payment is mind-blowing considering what is available on the market.
- I have installed with battery, that was really good because it was easy to install, but on the current pace (75% after 25 days) there is no way it will last the suggested 6 months on the website.

UPDATE: had to completely disable the motion sensor, the false positives were driving me crazy. Not paying the monthly fee. It's too many clicks to get to the screen when somebody actually pushes the button.
Avoid this product and wait for competitors to come up with something better.
UPDATE 2: Now this piece of crap will not enter live view.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation

Polk Audio ES35 Sound Wall Mount Speakers, Black & Polk Audio ES15 Wall Mount Bookshelf Speaker, Black I'm very pleased with all aspects of this center speaker. The sound quality is excellent. This replaces an old KEF center speaker and the difference can be clearly heard. The Polk has a crisp, clean sound that clarifies and enhances dialog but not at the expense of a nice solid bass (although I also have a subwoofer in the setup).

Aesthetically it's a simple, clean design. Normally I don't pay much attention to the look of a speaker but in this case, since it's a center speaker, it's in my line of sight all the time. It's about as unobtrusive you can get with a center speaker without compromising sound quality and performance. Polk did an excellent job with the design.

I looked at the new version of this (the ES35) and, while there are some small incremental improvements, I didn't consider them to be worth the extra $100 it costs. Plus, this was on a price dip for the differential between the two was $150, making this the clear choice.

While I have been partial to KEF in the past for speakers, the performance of this Polk has really wow'd me. At present I'm using this center speaker with KEF left and right front speakers, and KEF for surround. I've been so impressed with the ES35 that I'll be changing to Polk for my L/R soon, and keep the KEF only for surround (5.1.2 setup).

An excellent center speaker that hits the mark on all counts. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Polk Audio ES35 Sound Wall Mount Speakers, Black & Polk Audio ES15 Wall Mount Bookshelf Speaker, Black

I live in a very dusty area which in turn means constantly dusting out the internal components of the computer. The filter on the front of the case is a nice plus, it won't keep all the dust out but it will significantly reduce it which is great, meaning I won't have to clean out the insides as often as I used to.

The only problem I have with it is the 140 x 25 mm TriCool Fan on top is a bit more noisy than the rest of the fans but otherwise it's a fantastic case.

In closing: If you are looking for a new gaming case or just a new case in general, grab this one you won't regret it. Just don't forget some extra 120mm fans!

text_fidelity_a:
Audio-Technica ATH-LS50iSBK In-Ear Monitor Headphones with In-Line Mic & Control, Black As a disclaimer, I'm just an ordinary consumer (vs. a technical expert) when it comes to headphones, speakers, or earbuds. Having said that, here's my experience with these in-ear headphones:

As earbuds go, these are not as lightweight as the much cheaper, AmazonBasics and Panasonic ones I have owned. However, it's a weight difference that isn't really a problem, once I get them securely fastened around my ears.

The sound is wonderful. It has much more clarity than the inexpensive earbuds I usually buy. So to some extent the adage, "You get what you pay for," seems to apply here.

These earbuds have a useful extra: they have a microphone built in. Because of that, you can use it to speak on your cellphone, if you'd rather use this than a Bluetooth. Or if you are listening to entertainment media on your cell phone when you get a call, you won't have to unplug this earbud to take the call.

The microphone control has only one button, an on/off toggle switch. There are no volume adjustment buttons.

These earbuds seem to be well constructed. The cord is thicker and sturdier than my low-cost AmazonBasics and Panasonic earbuds.

The piece that fits into your ear has a relatively large casing compared to my other earbuds, but no doubt this is because the technology is more complicated.

These earbuds are an expensive buy for those of us who normally pay $7-12 for earbuds, but if you like to listen to music, it might be worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Audio-Technica ATH-LS50iSBK In-Ear Monitor Headphones with In-Line Mic & Control, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Streaming Stick+ | HD/4K/HDR Streaming Device with Long-range Wireless and Roku Voice Remote with TV Controls Overall, this is a very nice streaming system. The setup is pretty easy, although not nearly as quick and easy as the Fire TV since you have to register an account on Roku and give them a credit card (it is not charged unless you buy something).

I have it connected to an AV receiver and it's working great in terms of both picture and sound. The stick is slim enough to plug into an HDMI port on the back of the receiver without blocking anything. Wireless speed and connectivity is excellent.

What I don't like:
1. The four one-click buttons on the remote for Netflix, etc. can't be re-programmed. While the Netflix button is great since I have that service, the other 3 are useless. It would have been great to be able to reprogram them to work with an app of my choice.

2. The power and volume controls do NOT work with an AV receiver, only a TV. Since I have the stick plugged into my receiver, neither button is functional. Disappointing.

I also have a Fire TV box attached to the system. In comparison, the Roku menus are pretty dated looking as is the overall navigation. The remote is more clunky and doesn't respond as quickly at times. But, the Roku has apps that the Fire TV does not, so having both gives me more choices.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Streaming Stick+ | HD/4K/HDR Streaming Device with Long-range Wireless and Roku Voice Remote with TV Controls

When I plug in the keyboard, I simply take the cords down, hook up to the keyboard, and place the keyboard on my lap desk, using my favorite keyboard in front of the 65" screen.  Because I'm only using a keyboard and a mouse (my mouse plugs into a USB in the back of the keyboard and the 10' cable can also handle that bandwidth), I don't need anything higher than USB 2.0, and the 10 foot length doesn't affect the speed of the keyboard or mouse.  The cords are perfect!  They fit snugly into the USB ports on my laptop and also fit into my keyboard USB male end well at the USB extension's female end.  It's a great solution to allow me to use my favorite mechanical keyboard instead of a wireless non-mechanical keyboard at the TV.

ANTOP Omnidirectional HDTV Antenna Smartpass Amplified Outdoor 55/65 Miles Long Range AT-414B I've been collecting random TV antennas for review and from yard sales for years, and I think I've had about a dozen now. I generally only keep the two best ones. I tested this one out against my previous champion, which was just a single heavy duty rabbit ear on a magnetic base that somehow beat bigger, newer, and powered models.

The first thing I did with this when I got it was take it apart. I've gotten some in the past where the big plastic dish parts were just plastic for show and had nothing in them. Inside this one were multiple omnidirectional antennas and a circuit board. After attaching it to the coax, I checked through my channels and noticed I was missing some. I then added in the powered section, but didn't turn it on. This totally switched which channels I was missing. Then I turned it on and I got all my channels, plus another one I hadn't previously gotten, so it wins. The various parts do actually do something.

The pictures don't give much idea of scale. It's about the size of a steering wheel and comes with mounting plate. It's kind of huge and I wasn't pleased when I saw the size, but hey, I'll take the size if I get a brand new channel out of the deal.

I received a sample for review but the opinions are my own.

Like most others, I need my computer every day and I had no idea how long to expect the computer to be gone for shipping both ways and repair. Now the issue happens a lot more and I go to extremes to prevent it from sleeping.
Lesson learned, I will buy all future computers from local stores where my warranty can be handled without shipping mycomputer away for an undetermined amount of time.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation This is a great streaming box! Like the title says, it's a ROKU on steroids. I have an Apple Airport Extreme router and the ROKU would "occasionally" start buffering because of the processor; however, with the Amazon Fire TV, that's not an issue because it has a quad-core processor. Great streaming box!

Updated 5-4-14 I've had the Fire TV for a couple of months now and for the most part it's great; however, today we rented "Bad Grandpa" on Amazon. It played great but when there was 35 mins left in the movie, it quit playing. Tried to restart the movie and got a message saying there was a problem with playing the movie and to contact Amazon Customer Service. I called them and they said that when this happens, "...unplug the Fire TV for 15 seconds and then plug it back in." In my opinion, that takes the fun out of watching a movie! I thought the memory and quad-core processor would be enough to stop this from happening, wrong! Having said that, instead of naming my review "ROKU on Steroids" I should have named it "Just like ROKU".

The Amazon rep said that it was a problem with the memory of the Amazon Fire TV and not the video. When asked if the problem could be fixed by Amazon with an update, all he said was "I'll forward that to Amazon".

If you don't mind watching videos that stop playing and having to unplug the Fire TV and restart it during a movie, you'll really like the Fire TV.

One other point, the Amazon rep stated that it might be my router. I have an Apple Airport Extreme, the best and fastest available. If it was my router, I guess the Amazon rep should have had me unplug my router instead of the Fire TV. He finally admitted that it was the Fire TV and not the router.

Just wanted to get this information out there so people can be informed about the Amazon Fire TV before purchasing one. All in all, I'm happy with the Fire TV...just aggravated that I have to unplug it and restart it when watching movies. The Amazon Fire TV should be better than this!
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
WD 1TB Silver My Passport for Mac Portable External Hard Drive - USB 3.0 - WDBLUZ0010BSL-NESN Beside myself with joy. Backing up 775,000+ files with Time Machine could not have been easier.

This external drive was recommended by an Apple technician whom I hired to come tidy up the many issues that had developed over several years of working with my several Apple devices. While he was here, we called up Amazon and found the drive he recommended -- this one. It was promptly delivered. Connecting and running it could not have been easier. Feeling much more confident about continuing to work on my ancient MacBook.

UPDATE: This little guy has fallen on the tile flooring more times than I can count now. Amazingly, it hasn't broken yet. You should be aware that the connection to the cord that leads to your USB port is kind of loose -- especially where it plugs into the external drive. IO've had to use Scotch tape to secure it. Inelegant, but useful, BECAUSE...

Yesterday the client's gigantic file, replete with uncompressed images, crashed not only the file but my entire MS Wyrd program. Thanks to this little hard drive and Time Machine, Word was backed up -- although I didn't need to use the back-up to recover Word, the back-up could have been a life-saver. Time Machine failed to back up an uncorrupted version of the file recent enough to contain the six or eight hours' worth of edits I'd entered during that session. Ohhhh well... Not a function of the drive: a function of Apple's Time Machine.

I plan to buy another of these drives and manually back up current files, so as to have more than one copy of key data, one of which will always be unplugged from the machine.
///////

ADDENDUM: Made in Thailand, this little guy is tougher than one would expect. Because of a back problem, I can't sit at a desk; so, the external drive has been attached to a MacBook that allows me to work in pain-free seating. This entails my hauling the computer array around with me to more than one seating arrangement, and lifting the junk on and off of various nearby tables. I've dropped it several times and each time expected it would be dead. No: it survived a half-dozen drops on tile floor before I figured out that I could tape the cable into the Passport connection. Last night, though, a fairly mild tap (not a drop!) did it in. I'm ordering two more, so that I can switch them out every other day; that way, the next time I break one, I'll have a backup to the backup.

The connection between the USB cable and the Passport comes apart readily. You can remedy that -- not aesthetically but effectively -- with a piece of Scotch tape.
text_fidelity_b: WD 1TB Silver My Passport for Mac Portable External Hard Drive - USB 3.0 - WDBLUZ0010BSL-NESN

Verso Prologue Case Cover for Kindle Fire, Tan (does not fit Kindle Fire HD) At first glance, this appears to be an elegant folio cover for tablets; it has an authentic-looking antique book design with embossing on the faux leather, some "gold" leafing, and real top-stitching, and it fits nicely on a book shelf (great disguise if you think you need to hide your device for whatever reason). While the design is lovely and the black microfiber supposedly prevents your screen from getting scratched, the way the tablet is held in is by four elastic straps that do an ok job, but I feel in time will wear out. Because of that concern, the design gets 4/5 stars

The function of this folio is to give the tablet a different look and ease of portability without fear of it breaking. It also helps serve as a dust cover for those who have tablets that don't always use them. This is not made for all terrain, though it's good and light weight enough for public transport. Parks and other minor recreational places are ok. I wouldn't take this folio camping or to the beach do to fear of destroying both the folio and tablet. Even though there is a cover there is a minor opening that doesn't really stay closed with the tablet in it. This folio doesn't really appear to protect a tablet from accidental drops. For every day use, this gets a 3.5/5, and for not-so every day use (rougher environments), it's closer to 1/5, so bear that in mind when deciding what case to buy.

The positive thing about this folio is that it fits most 7.1 inch tablets It did fit the Galaxy Tab 7.1 and the original kindle with keyboard. I would recommend an accessories pack to go along with the folio, since screen protector is a must! Over all for a folio I would give it 3.5/5 rounded up to 4. While is is beautiful, it only keeps to the basics of what a tablet user needs.
text_fidelity_b: Verso Prologue Case Cover for Kindle Fire, Tan (does not fit Kindle Fire HD)

Belkin N300 Wireless N Router (Latest Generation) (F9K1002) Bought this for my mother who has a small 2 bedroom apartment. Has been installed for over 3 weeks now. It was so very easy to install, simple instructions, did not have to adjust any settings. We just attached it to the DSL modem, loaded the CD into each computer that was going to use the network, followed the simple instructions, works great. We did have a problem trying to set up an account, which we still have not been able to do. May call later for assistance if we find it would be helpful to have an account, but so far everything works great.

We have had my mother's desktop computer (also running wireless now), her notebook computer, my notebook computer and the printer all running on the network at the same time. There was absolutely no degradation in service, have never had a problem with disconnects even with all computers running at the same time and two of the computers sending documents to the printer. This includes using one of the notebook computers at the furthest location in the apartment away from the router as possible. The only problem we have is the slower Verizon DSL service compared to the faster Verizon FIOS service I have at my house, so not a Belkin problem. Too bad my mother can't get FIOS. But her internet access is as fast as it was when it was attached directly to the modem.

Would highly recommend this product.

5/28/2015 - Just found this review I wrote in 2011. My mother is still using the same Belkin N150, still works great even if we have 3 computers running at the same time. The retirement community she lives in switched voice/Internet carriers about 6 months ago. Saw no difference in performance. Highly recommend.

Logitech MX Master 3S for Mac Wireless Bluetooth Mouse, Ultra-Fast Scrolling, Ergo, 8K DPI, Quiet Clicks, Track on Glass, USB-C, Apple, iPad - Space Grey - With Free Adobe Creative Cloud Subscription I’m really picky when it comes to mice. I usually end up with a gaming mouse because they are comfortable and fulfill my needs. But because I use a Mac, it’s rare that I can customize buttons and macros and all that.

So I was really excited to try out the Logitech MX Master 3. I’ve been using it for the past month and keep going back to it. I have two work spaces in my house, and I find myself taking the mouse from desk to desk, instead of using what’s already on the desk.

The mouse feels nice in my hand. I have small hands (size small in gloves), and the mouse nestles nicely against my palm. My fingers don’t have to stretch to reach any of the buttons. The thumb rest is comfortable. I only wish the mouse had better pinky support.

The scroll wheel … I love the scroll wheel. Logitech calls it the “MagSpeed™ Electromagnetic” scroll wheel which is a really fancy way of saying it scrolls like butter. The wheel is nearly silent and super precise. It has just the right amount of feedback when scrolling slowly through a page, and flies when I want to get to the bottom of a long article. It really is a joy to use.

The mouse charges via USB-C and includes a USB-C to USB-C cable. I couldn’t try out the Flow option, where you can copy/paste text, images, and files between computers because my other Mac’s version of iOS is too old to install Logitech Options. But I was able to connect the mouse to both of my Macs and switch between them using the 1, 2, 3 button on the bottom.

Logitech Options offers a decent amount of customization. You can customize settings across all applications, such as pointer and scrolling speed. Some of the buttons can be customized: gesture, scroll wheel click, wheel shift, horizontal scroll, back, and forward.

App specific options can be assigned to the buttons. Defaults are assigned for the most popular programs like Chrome and Photoshop, and I was able to add customizations for my personal favorite, Scrivener.

But what I don’t like is that I’m limited in picking what the buttons can do. I really wanted to change the horizontal scroll wheel into another vertical scroll wheel, but I can’t. I can only do the functions Logitech thinks I want, such as zooming or navigating between tabs.

The MX Master 3 has a lot of nice functions and has been designed for productivity. I’ve barely touched on a lot of what you can do with this mouse.

I just wish I could customize *everything* because what I need for productivity doesn’t match what someone else needs, or what Logitech assumes I want.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Master 3S for Mac Wireless Bluetooth Mouse, Ultra-Fast Scrolling, Ergo, 8K DPI, Quiet Clicks, Track on Glass, USB-C, Apple, iPad - Space Grey - With Free Adobe Creative Cloud Subscription
