Garmin vívofit 2 Activity Tracker, White The circumference of my wrist is 5 1/4 inches above the bone which is fairly small and the small wristband fits perfectly, there are still 5 holes (1.5 inches) left to make it smaller.

The two reasons I went for this activity tracker are it is waterproof and the battery lasts one year... for me these are the most important reasons because I really hate all this constant charging of gadgets.

Syncing is easy, at the end of the day I just press one button and it syncs with my smartphone, it also comes with a little blue-tooth USB attachment if you want to sync it with your computer. I've read they will add autosync with the next software update which is supposed to arrive shortly.

You get to choose what to see on your screen when you press the button, I went with steps, goal, distance and time. You can also add the date, calories and heart rate if you are wearing a strap.

I absolutely love how it feels, it doesn't bother me at all, you don't have to wear it real tight and the silicon is very soft.

The reason I took one star off is that the beep sound which comes on after one hour of inactivity (when the red warning line appears) is way, way, way too quiet. I set an alarm just to check on the beep sound and it was so short and subtle, if there would be any kind of background noise you won't be able to hear it at all.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin vívofit 2 Activity Tracker, White

WD 2TB Elements Portable HDD, External Hard Drive, USB 3.0 for PC & Mac, Plug and Play Ready - WDBU6Y0020BBK-WESN 09/09/2020 update:
Last 2 4T harddrives that I have purchased from Amazon have been defective. The male end of the cord would not seamlessly fit into the female portion of the hard drive. Both returned. I am purchased directly from WD from this point forward. BE VERY CAREFUL. IF CORD DOES NOT FIT SEAMLESSLY and the female end is not lining up perfectly for the male end . . . DO NOT USE IT AND RETURN!

8/15/2020:
In 15 years, I have had 2 laptops crash. And 1 desktop crash in that amount of time. But - I have never lost information. I don't store my information on my desktop or laptop . . . I worked solely off of harddrives. I have used the WD Elements Hard Drives for over 15 years now. I had 1 4tb that I used over and over again to back up my laptop and personal files. As I got busier with work and life . . . fast forward 15 years and I now have 6 of these. I work daily off of 2 of these . . . one has personal files and the other has work files. No delay. That being said . . . my desktop has a top of the line processor, but I don't think that works to make the hard drive move any faster. But still . . . I work all day every day without any delays . . .

I have 2 backups of the original working harddrives - for work and for personal. I back up every single week like clockwork.

I then have 2 backups of the 1st backups. You don't want to be backing up your working harddrive (thereby putting into play your original harddrive and your 1st back up harddrive) . . . so you need a 2nd back up in the event something catastrophic occurs during the back up of your original harddrives. So I have 3 each for work (1 I work off of every day) and 3 each for personal (1 I work off of every day).

I know that I will always have a full set of my work files, my Outlook files and my accounting files.

Yep . . . it's a $600 investment for peace of mind and security of my files . . . and it's a system that works for me . . .

I have used other harddrives by WD and I personally don't care for them. I especially dislike the wifi / icloud ones. These elements are so easy . . . just plug it in and go. Or in my case . . . plug them in and work all day every day.

text_fidelity_a:
iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice This is a pretty mixed review of an interesting concept that is pretty good right now, but has the potential to be great in the near future. At the current price of about $150, this is ok+ based on the following criteria:

Sound Quality: 2.5-3 stars
For the size, it's ok
When reviewing for sound quality, I compare speakers (and headphones) to comparably sized items, based on speakers I currently or previously have owned. I take price range *somewhat* into account (I don't expect $15 headphones to sound like $500 ones), but for anything over $100, I use the full range from the cheapest stuff I have, to my favorite brand, Bose.
So with that in mind, I have a portable wireless Bose speaker that is smaller and acts as the "5" on the scale.
The sound on this can get loud enough to not distort and still fill a smallish room or normal bedroom fine. The treble and bass are ok, though the higher ranges are tinny and the bass lacks depth. Overall sound from high to low and throughout the mid range lack definition. It's good enough for very casual background listening and for podcasts.

Alexa Feature: 4 stars
I have an iPhone and think Alexa has quite a bit more understanding and skill than Siri. When asked questions, from simple stuff like "what's the weather" to more complicated stuff like "I'm hungry. What can I make in half an hour?", the answers and follow-up questions are highly intuitive and thorough. Does she get everything all the time? No. But she does a much better job than Siri.

User-Friendliness: 2.5 stars
I didn't like the process of figuring out how this works, particularly the part of pairing with more than one device and also Having to use an app to make most of it work. It was a clunky, irritating process that more or less stayed that way every time I wanted to use this thing, especially for listening to music. It should be able to just play from your iTunes through the iTunes app and bluetooth, and instead, I was only able to make it play iTunes though Their App, which sucks when it comes to my music. And that brings us to the App..

App: 2 stars
No. Just no. Bluetooth exists for a reason, and if a speaker has bluetooth, you should be able to just pair and play. I had to use the app to play from my iTunes, and because I have a very specific way of organizing things, I was incredibly annoyed that something didn't translate, and my music was disorganized and basically impossible to search for with this app. Instead of being able to play what I want from one of my playlist subfolders, it disregarded my way of organizing things, and I ended up giving up. If I can't listen to my stuff easily with this, then like 75% of the reason to use this disappears, leaving me with an expensive alarm clock with weather report, recipe ideas, and some cool internet stuff. That's cool, but it's quite incomplete for what I need, and what I suspect many people want.

tl;dr version: sound is mediocre but doable, app is bad, Alexa is super clever and smart, and the experience has a lot of frustrating aspects.
text_fidelity_b: iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice

Most of the band name speakers were around $100 but this one stood out from the cheap chinese models. It had similar specs and build quality much more expensive brands. I tried it out for myself for a week before handing it off to my mom.

I was impressed with the soundstage this speaker projected. Highs and mids were crisp and clear without be drowned out by the bass. Spoken word comes through crisp and clear, even at high volume levels. Even with the volume maxed out, playing hard thumping EDM, there was minimal distortion. The connection time to your phone is a tad slow but not bad. Battery life seems great. I really like that it can charge other devices via USB in an emergency. This speaker seems like it would be fine if tipped over, dropped from short heights, or left out in the rain by accident. My only disappointment was a lack of bluetooth volume sync. Higher end speakers let sync your device's volume to the speaker so chaining volume from either your phone or speaker changes both.

My mom is happy with how simple and easy it is to use. There aren't a ton of buttons and options. You turn it on, control the volume, or play/pause. It gets plenty loud enough to fill the room with her favorite music and doesn't overwhelm her with options.

This would be a great speaker for an older relative or younger child who's comfortable using basic smartphone apps to find music and wants a simple, good sounding and durable speaker.

1. These headphones are really different in appearance from regular earbud-type headphones, but they are oddly attractive in their design.

2. They are great for swimming in a pool or in any outdoor body of water, because they are extensively waterproof. They can be submerged to a depth of 20 meters (65 feet). This means they can be used for snorkeling and scuba diving.

6. A built-in microphone allows you to use the Bluetooth function to place and received calls on your cell phone.

7. These headphones are lightweight, durable, and flexible.

CONS

1. Other than for water sports and for safety purposes, these headphones are not as good as regular earbuds, because their sound quality is comparatively quite inferior.

2. Compared to regular Bluetooth earbuds, their price is very high.

PixelFlash No-Bend Pins USB 3 CF Card Reader, Compact Flash Card Reader, Tactical SuperSpeed CompactFlash Memory Adapter, Rugged Anti-Scratch Exterior Classic Card Reader - White I love it when a product does exactly what it should do, and does it very well. I can't say that about many of the PC add-ons I use, but I can say that for this CF card reader. It works great and is easy to use. Perfect!

I use CF cards mainly to hold and transfer MP3 files to my car (it has a CF card reader, for some reason, built into the stereo). I've killed a couple of cheap CF card readers by not taking care when inserting the card, and bending a pin. The Pixelflash reader is designed so the card fits deep into the reader, making it pretty much impossible to bend a pin.

Other pluses include a non-slip type coating so it's easy to grip. It also gives it a nice quality feel. The only downside is that, due to the deep design, it's wide (about 2.5 inches at the widest point), and can block more than one USB port if they are close together.

The speed is excellent. I'm using it on a USB 2.0 port, and found it transferred a directory of a hundred-odd songs nearly twice as fast as my old reader using the same card (a Ridata). I don't have a USB3.0 port to use it on, but when I upgrade to that I imagine the speed will be even better.

Installation was a no-brainer. Just plugged it in and Win 7 (32 bit) recognized it immediately. Also used it on an XP (SP3) machine with the same plug-and-play ease.

Easy to use, great speed, and 3.0 compatible for future needs. Highly recommend!

[I received a reader from the manufacturer for review purposes]

text_fidelity_a:
Sonpre Samurai Max-C Pop-up SD Rechargeable Speaker for Smartphones/Laptops/Tablets/MP3s - Black This is a more upscale version of the “pop up” speakers that have been around for a while. It adds some useful features including an SD card slot to play mp3 files directly and more advanced controls, such as a toggle switch for track skip and a mute button.

When compressed it’s very compact, measuring roughly 2.5 inches in diameter. While it can be played in its compact mode, the sound quality is not all that great – very tinny with little bass.

The sound quality improves significantly when it’s popped open. That increases the height to about 3.25 inches. That doesn't seem like much, but it makes a huge difference in sound quality. The bass is far more pronounced and, while the mid and upper ranges are still somewhat muddy, it’s far more pleasant to listen to than when it is folded up.

Given the size, I’d rate the sound quality as very good when it is in its pop-up mode. This is not a room-filling speaker but it sounds a whole lot better than the internal speakers in a tablet.

It is a direct-connect only speaker – it does NOT have bluetooth. It comes with a 3.5mm cord that is permanently attached to the base of the speaker. The cable can be stowed in a grove on the base of the speaker. The attached cable is a plus and a minus: you’ll never forget to bring a cable along, but the cord is only about 5 inches long, which made it backward to use on some of my equipment. I like that the cord is attached, but it really needs to be a bit longer.

The build quality feels pretty solid. It’s all plastic, as expected, but it has a nice feel to it. The bellows section in the middle feels like it is build solid enough to last a while. Plus, the fact that you can close it up easily for transport gives me some measure of assurance that it will survive being tossed around a bit. For the price, I’d rate the build quality as very good.

There are less expensive pop-up speakers available, such as the Xboom. I have one of those as well, and when comparing the two side-by-side I thought the sound quality was bit better on the Sonpre. The Sonpre also has more features than the Xboom (the mute button in particular is a welcome addition) and has longer battery life. So, while it is a few bucks more, it does bring some additional features to the table.

Although the short cord drops my rating by a star, this is definitely one to consider if you’re looking for a decent sounding pop-up speaker.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Sonpre Samurai Max-C Pop-up SD Rechargeable Speaker for Smartphones/Laptops/Tablets/MP3s - Black
